verified.exploit_entry_point: The repository's public reference surface after PlainInit / git.Init: storing, reading and removing a reference through the storage interface, the reflog storer, and Repository.Tag / DeleteTag. Hidden tests open real repositories with git.PlainInit (osfs) and, for the second write implementation, filesystem.NewStorage over a backend whose Capabilities lack ReadAndWrite.
sites: storage/filesystem/dotgit/dotgit.go:1047 SetRef (write dispatcher entry; covers the second implementation behind it)
repository.go:1032-1053 Tag / DeleteTag (short name normalised with path.Join before the storage sees it)
routes: T1: store 'config' (aliases .git/config with no traversal), 'refs/../../config', 'hooks/pre-commit'; checked on both write implementations
T4: read 'hooks/post-checkout' (metadata aliased as a reference) and 'refs/../../config'
T5: append to the reflog of 'refs/../../config'; read and delete a reflog named '../hooks/post-checkout'
T6: Tag('../heads/main') returns a branch and DeleteTag('../heads/main') deletes it; DeleteTag('../../config') removes the configuration file
verified.project_tests_run: go test ./storage/filesystem/dotgit ./storage/filesystem ./plumbing -count=1 (pinned, oracle, alternative, hardening and every check patch; Go 1.26.4)

traps.shape: a stored reference name resolves onto unrelated repository metadata or climbs out of the reference tree; the same rule must hold on both write implementations (the common one and the simpler one chosen when a backend cannot open files read-write); coupled: nested refs and root pseudo-references keep storing and reading
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the write looks like the application's own repository data, and checking only for parent-path components looks sufficient until a name such as 'config' aliases metadata with no traversal at all
traps.realistic_because: published fix site; the second write implementation is the reader's T2

traps.shape: the second write implementation selected for filesystems without read-write capability performs the same name-to-path join with no check; guarding only the common backend leaves it open
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it exists only for simple filesystems that cannot open files read-write and is documented as single-process, so it reads as the caller's own trusted backend
traps.realistic_because: published fix site: the published fix guards the dispatcher above both implementations, so a solver who guards only the common one misses it

traps.shape: a removal by a name that aliases metadata or carries a parent-path component removes unrelated repository data
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the delete path is reached only after an existence check on the same name, which looks like proof that the name is a stored reference

traps.shape: a read by such a name returns unrelated repository data as a reference value
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the read returns no file content to the caller, only a parsed reference or an error, so it looks harmless

traps.shape: the three reflog operations on the sibling logs directory join the same name with no validation
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reflog storer is a low-level surface for names the caller already owns, and its directory is separate from the reference tree

traps.shape: a public tag operation normalises the caller's short name into a reference path before the storage check, so a short name that walks to a legitimate branch resolves and is acted on instead of being refused
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the neighbouring create path validates its short name, so the read and delete pair looks covered, and the name the storage finally sees is a perfectly ordinary reference name
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the later upstream change removes the same normalisation

traps.shape: the containment rule must not become a refs/-prefix or existing-validator rule: the layer accepts single-component names, root pseudo-references, the partial-clone placeholder, symbolic targets and reflogs under logs/HEAD
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the neighbouring placeholder-looking names invite a rule that refuses them
traps.realistic_because: each value is a legitimate use exercised by the pinned project's own storage suite

patch_checks.why: fresh agent (deepseek-flash[1m]), full view (instruction, tree, tests, reference, trap list)

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: every refusal returns an error; a crash would abort the Go test binary instead of reading as a clean refusal
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: there are no roles, peers or directions; every caller uses the same storage interface
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: no identity or credential is parsed; the guarded value is a reference name
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: there is no authority lookup whose empty answer could fail open

A.summary: adds a lexical reference-name containment check at the six storage sinks on the v6 line

B.summary: the same protection, stricter (refs/-or-root-pseudo-ref policy), applied to the v5 tree
